The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 07-04-2023 at about 5.30p.m. he was driving an Auto- rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-07/A-4558 with three passengers on Nangali-Mulbagal NH-75 Road, he stopped the said rickshaw at Kappalamadagu Village Bus Stop to alight the passenger, at that time, the driver of the Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-07/B-5086 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, dashed to the petitioner's Auto and caused the accident.
As a result of forced impact, petitioner and other passengers were fell down and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital and admitted as an inpatient, the petitioner sustained closed left monteggia fracture and underwent surgery.

Other injuries treated with conservatively, the petitioner is still under treatment, he was spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical and other expenses.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, he is completely bed ridden and cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident.
4. It is further stated that at the time of accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 38 years, he was working as Auto Driver at his own vehicle and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-p.m.
Due to the injuries, he is not able to do his job and lost his earnings.

5. It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero vehicle bearing No.KA-07/B-5086, against whom the Mulbagal Rural Police have registered the case in Cr.No.104/2023 P/U/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.

Hence,
respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and they have filed objection to the main petition.
7. Respondent No.1 in its objection has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and it is liable to be dismissed in limine.

sentences.text: It is no doubt true as per - Ex.R.1 an endorsement issued by the RTO, the fitness certificate of the offending vehicle was not in force as on the date of accident.
If that is so the insurer should not have insured the vehicle for the period during which vehicle did not possess the fitness certificate.

The insurer cannot say they would insure a vehicle irrespective of the fact that whether it has a fitness certificate or not and collect premium and when it comes to liability, their liability is subject to vehicle possessing fitness certificate.

It is in this background, a Division Bench of this Court in the case of The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Sri.N.Srinivasa Murthy and others MFA No.6621/2006 c.w. MFA CROB No.304/2006 has held, that the vehicle not having fitness certificate cannot be a reason for the insurance company to deny compensation to the claimant.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Sri.N.Srinivasa Murthy and others MFA No.6621/2006 c.w. MFA CROB No.304/2006
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The facts of this case are identical to the facts involved in MFA No.6621/2006 c.w. MFA CROB No.304/2006 and therefore the matter is fully covered by the said judgment of division bench.
9. The life of an insurance policy issued in respect of a motor vehicle will be valid for one year and for every next year either it has to be renewed or new policy has to be obtained.

Therefore, the insurer at every time of insuring a vehicle and issuing policy or renewing such policy should verify whether the vehicle has possessed all the necessary certificates including the fitness certificate.

The insurance companies cannot blindly insure motor vehicles and collect premium and thereafter contend that the vehicle did not possess fitness certificate at the relevant point of time and therefore they are not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
This attitude of the insurer cannot be encouraged any longer.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified.
The insurer is directed to pay compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
It is open for the insurer to initiate separate proceedings and recover compensation from the owner of the offending vehicle.

On perusal of the ratio laid down in the said judgment, it is clear that, once insurance policy has been issued by the insurer, it cannot take the defence of non- availability of valid documents like Suresha vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192092294/
9 F.C. and Permit.

sentences.text: As per the ratio laid down in the above judgment, it is clear that, if Vehicle is duly insured, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

Therefore, it is clear that, if insurance company has issued the insurance policy and it is valid as on the date of accident, it has to pay the compensation to the victims and it may recover it from the owner of the vehicle.

Therefore,
in the present case though there is no valid Permit to the offending vehicle, respondent No.1 ought to have pay the compensation and recover it from the owner.

42. This Tribunal relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior in Misc. Appeal No.5812/2024 between Cholamandala MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Munni Bai & Others,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court held at Para No.8 that ......
8. ......
...... The insurance policy is a statutory contract entered into between the insurer and the insured for the benefit of the third party.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Cholamandala MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Munni Bai & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the insured has violated the conditions of the insurance policy, it is a matter between the insurer and the insured, and the third party cannot be made to suffer by going for execution against a private person instead of the insurer.

Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, Paragraph 102(x) of the judgment in the case of Swaran Singh (supra) would apply even if the proviso to sub-section 4 and sub-section 5 of Section 149 of Act has been omitted, and that has not brought any difference in the application of the principle of pay and recover.

Therefore, on perusal of the above ratio, this Court is of the opinion that, even after Amended Act 2019, the liability of respondent No.1/insurance company is not taken away and it is still under the obligation of indemnify the owners risk and recover the same from its insured.
43. Hence, from the evidence available on record it can be held that the policy in force for which Respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner respondent No.2.

Hence,
respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner and insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer shall indemnify respondent No.2 in payment of compensation amount to the petitioners and later it can be recovered from the owner.
44. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shamanna and another V/s.

The Divisional Manager,
The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others (2018 (9) SCC 650) wherein it is held that there is duty on the part of the insurer to satisfy the award on the basis of principle of pay and recover.

In the above decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the tribunal shall follow the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Swaran Singh ((2004) 3 SCC 297) and national Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Laxmi Narain Dhut ((2007) 3 SCC 700)
and adopt the principle of pay and recover.

sentences.text: 46. Therefore, as discussed above, in this case the petitioner was the third party to the offending vehicle and as such due to no fault, the petitioner cannot be denied from availing benefit of compensation towards the injuries to the petitioner in the motor vehicle accident.

Therefore, as per the dictum laid down in the said citations, This Tribunal has power to grant compensation by applying the principle of pay and recover and insurance company is liable to pay the compensation first and recover the same from the owner as per the award passed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
47. ISSUE No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,02,274/- with interest @ 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondents No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount.
Further, respondent No.1 shall indemnify respondent No.2 and shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Respondent No.1 shall recover the same from the respondent No.2.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

...... The insurance policy is a statutory contract entered into between the insurer and the insured for the benefit of the third party.
If the insured has violated the conditions of the insurance policy, it is a matter between the insurer and the insured, and the third party cannot be made to suffer by going for execution against a private person instead of the insurer.
Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, Paragraph 102(x) of the judgment in the case of Swaran Singh (supra) would apply even if the proviso to sub-section 4 and sub-section 5 of Section 149 of Act has been omitted, and that has not brought any difference in the application of the principle of pay and recover.
Therefore, on perusal of the above ratio, this Court is of the opinion that, even after Amended Act 2019, the liability of respondent No.1/insurance company is not taken away and it is still under the obligation of indemnify the owners risk and recover the same from its insured.
